title: Swahili Fish Stew with Cassava
community: Coastal Tanzania — the complete coastal one-pot meal
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Mchuzi wa Samaki na Muhogo — fish and cassava simmered together in a fragrant coconut milk and spice sauce. The complete one-pot coastal meal — fish for protein, cassava for starch, coconut milk for richness.
longDesc: Fish and cassava stew is the complete coastal meal — protein, starch, and sauce in one pot. The cassava absorbs the coconut-spice sauce completely, becoming extraordinarily rich and flavourful alongside the fish.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, spices, tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes.
Add cassava pieces and ½ cup water. Cover and cook 15 minutes until partially tender.
Add coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fish. Cover and simmer gently 12—15 minutes.
Cassava should be completely tender; fish should flake easily.
chefTips: Add cassava before fish — it takes much longer.
Do not stir once fish is added — it breaks apart.
cookingScience: Cassava starch gelatinises into the coconut milk during cooking, naturally thickening the sauce. This is why no additional thickening is needed — the cassava does the work.
sustainabilityTips: Cassava is one of Tanzania's most climate-resilient crops.
culturalNote: Fish and cassava stew is the complete coastal meal — protein from the sea and starch from the land, united by the coconut milk that makes everything better on the Swahili coast.
